Team — reviewed Novus’ redline and provided suggested redlines in the attached markup. Summary of our position and rationale below.

1) Liability cap: propose mutual cap tied to fees (12 months of Fees or $3,000,000, whichever is greater). Rationale: 24 months is outside our standard enterprise exposure band and materially increases reserve risk. A floor protects us on low-fee pilots while keeping the cap meaningful for Novus.

2) Exclusions from cap: maintain carve-outs for (a) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (b) breaches of confidentiality/data obligations, (c) intellectual property indemnity obligations, and (d) payment obligations. These are standard and protect core legal/financial risk.

3) SLA credits and sole remedy language: Novus requests credits to offset monetary liability under the cap. We should avoid credits that reduce the liability cap dollar-for-dollar. Recommended compromise: (a) include an explicit "service credits are the exclusive financial remedy for SLA failures up to X% of monthly fees (describe schedule)" clause; (b) state that service credits do not reduce or count toward the liability cap, but also make clear that acceptance of credits is the sole monetary remedy for SLA-specific service degradations — i.e., the customer cannot claim both credits and additional monetary damages for the same SLA failure (no double recovery). This maintains predictable unit economics while addressing Novus’ desire for credits.

4) Credit cap mechanics: recommend limiting annual aggregate credits to a percentage of annual fees (e.g., 20% of annual fees) with per-incident caps as per our SLA schedule. This bounded mechanism gives Novus meaningful relief while preventing open-ended offset exposure.

5) Remedy hierarchy & mutual remedies: include a sentence that termination for uncured material breach remains available and that certain injunctive remedies (e.g., for data exposure) are not displaced by the sole remedy clause.

6) Practical negotiation posture: offer the 12-month or $3M floor cap + credit mechanics above. If Novus insists on 24 months, consider commercial offset: increase initial commitment term or modest discount in exchange for higher cap.

I’ve attached Redwood_Proposed_Liability_Markup.docx with exact text. If you want, I can prepare a redline that explicitly shows credits "not reducing the cap" language to send to Novus.

High level: Redwood can move on a mutual liability cap but at 12 months of fees (with a $3M floor).
